# An exact, executable reproduction of the known integral heptagon

The existence question recorded in the prompt has a positive answer due to Tobias Kreisel and Sascha Kurz (2008). Their distance matrix(1) and Figure1 provide the following seven points. Write a coordinate pair$(a,b)$ for the actual Euclidean point$(a,b\sqrt{2002})$:
\[
\begin{split}
&(0,0),\ (22270,0),\
(26127018/2227,932064/2227),\\
&(245363/17,3144/17),\
(17615968/2227,238464/2227),\\
&(56068/17,3144/17),\
(19079044/2227,-54168/2227).
\end{split}
\]
The original coordinates need not be integral. Every pairwise distance is an integer, with matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
0&22270&22098&16637&9248&8908&8636\\
22270&0&21488&11397&15138&20698&13746\\
22098&21488&0&10795&14450&13430&20066\\
16637&11397&10795&0&7395&11135&11049\\
9248&15138&14450&7395&0&5780&5916\\
8908&20698&13430&11135&5780&0&10744\\
8636&13746&20066&11049&5916&10744&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The attached standard-library program checks the coordinates against every upper-triangular matrix entry as an exact equality
\[
(a_i-a_j)^2+2002(b_i-b_j)^2=D_{ij}^2.
\]
It then checks every triple and quadruple, rather than relying on a drawing. For a triple, nonvanishing of the determinant with rows$(a_i,b_i,1)$ is equivalent to noncollinearity after multiplying the second coordinate by$\sqrt{2002}$. For a quadruple, test the determinant with rows
\[
(a_i^2+2002b_i^2,\ a_i,\ b_i,\ 1).
\]
Its nonvanishing is equivalent to the standard Euclidean circle determinant being nonzero, since the latter differs by the nonzero column factor$\sqrt{2002}$. All entries of the tested determinants are rational. Exact Gaussian elimination with fractions therefore avoids both floating error and arithmetic in an unspecified algebraic-number package.

The executed checker passed all21 distance equalities, all35 triple tests and all35 quadruple tests. The largest displayed distance is22270. It rejects optimized Python execution so that assertions cannot silently disappear; execution records and program hash are retained. This is a complete finite certificate of the displayed configuration's properties, supplemented by the determinant equivalences just proved. It is not an exhaustive search over configurations.

Kreisel–Kurz also state minimality of diameter22270 in Theorem1 using an exhaustive search. That search has not been rerun here, so this report does not independently certify their diameter-minimality theorem. The contribution is a reproducible exact certificate for the known affirmative existence result, with source credit and the precise general-position interpretation; neither convex position nor integer coordinates is asserted.
